Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, our CEO; Sarah Chen, our CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, our CTO; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.  

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a pivotal quarter for Voltara Motors. We made significant strides in key areas, including our electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains, revenue growth from software and services like subscriptions and autonomous driving features, gross margin expansion through cost discipline and scale, and robust profitability in our energy business. We delivered 120,000 vehicles globally, up 45% year-over-year, while advancing our leadership in sustainable mobility. We are particularly excited about the upcoming launch of the Voltara Two platform and its anticipated impact on our market share, targeting over 500 miles of EPA range and new bidirectional capabilities.  

These achievements position us strongly in a competitive landscape. Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to discuss our financial performance in more detail.  

Sarah Chen:  
Thank you, Elena, and good morning, everyone. For Q3, our total revenue reached $6.8 billion, representing a 52% increase year-over-year. Automotive revenue was $5.2 billion, with energy adding $1.6 billion. Our consolidated gross margin was 24.2%, up 580 basis points from last year. Operating expenses were $1.1 billion, reflecting disciplined investments in R&D and scaling. Net income came in at $520 million, or $0.85 per diluted share. We are maintaining a strong balance sheet with $4.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for Q4 calls for revenue of $7.5 to $8.0 billion, automotive gross margins of 24.5 to 25.0%, and continued energy growth.  

Today, I'd like to dive deeper into some of our fastest-growing and highest-margin segments, starting with software and services. This area continues to transform Voltara from a hardware-focused OEM into a software-defined vehicle leader. In Q3, software and services generated $620 million in revenue, up 162% year-over-year and 28% quarter-over-quarter. On a run-rate basis, that's approaching $2.5 billion annualized, now making up 18% of our total automotive revenue—more than double the 7% from a year ago.  

Breaking it down, subscription revenue hit $410 million. Premium Connectivity, which includes unlimited supercharging, live traffic visualization using our proprietary high-definition maps, and streaming services, brought in $180 million. Average revenue per user rose to $12 per month, a 25% increase year-over-year, boosted by bundling with Sentry Mode Pro for advanced security analytics. The In-Car Entertainment Suite, with AR/VR gaming and personalized AI assistants, added $110 million, reaching adoption rates of 35% across our 2.8 million vehicle installed base.  

Our Autonomous Driving Suite, ADS 3.0—our SAE Level 3-capable system for highway autonomy—generated $210 million, including $140 million from new subscriptions and upgrades, plus $70 million from one-time feature unlocks. We've activated it on over 450,000 vehicles worldwide, with a 42% take-rate among eligible owners, up from 28% last quarter. This leverages our neural network architecture, trained on more than 15 billion miles of real-world fleet data. Gross margins here are outstanding at 88%, enabled by over-the-air delivery and our scalable Dojo 2.0 supercomputer cluster, expanded with NVIDIA H100 GPUs to reduce inference costs by 40%.  

Regionally, North America drove 62% of this revenue at $385 million, supported by NHTSA's updated ADAS framework and high uptake among our premium models. China contributed $155 million or 25%, growing 210% year-over-year despite competition from XPeng and Baidu, thanks to localized HD maps via our Baidu joint venture and WeChat integration—ARPU there hits $15 per month, the region's highest. Europe added $60 million or 10%, with conservative growth amid data privacy rules, but our Berlin OTA hub has sped activations by 30%. The rest of the world, including Australia and Middle East pilots, is 3% but grew 300% year-over-year.  

Strategically, our custom ElectroNet chips handle 95% of autonomy compute in-house, cutting latency below 50 milliseconds. Customer lifetime value has jumped to $18,000 over eight years, versus $4,500 for hardware alone, with churn under 2% from our ecosystem lock-in. Acquisition cost payback is now under three months, far better than rivals. Looking forward, we're aiming for a $1 billion Q4 run-rate, with ADS 4.0 beta-testing next month on 50,000 Robotaxi prototypes. We've filed for unsupervised FSD approvals in California and Texas, and V2G subscriptions could add $100 million in the first half of 2025. This 85% EBITDA-margin flywheel fuels investments in LFP batteries and our Supercharger network expansion to 60,000 stalls globally.  

Shifting to our energy business, which is evolving into a core profitability engine. This segment, including Megapack utility-scale storage, Powerwall for residential and commercial use, and solar-plus-storage solutions, posted $1.6 billion in revenue—up 162% year-over-year and 45% sequentially. Deployments reached 12.4 GWh, a 185% increase, powered by record output from Shanghai Gigafactory 3 and our new Lathrop facility in California. Revenue mix favored Megapack at 78% or $1.25 billion, up 195%; Powerwall and C&I at 18% or $288 million, up 112%; and solar products like Solar Roof 3.0 at 4% or $64 million, up 89%. Our backlog stands at $28 billion, with 85% weighted to 2025-2026.  

Profitability was exceptional, with energy gross profit at $448 million and a 28.0% gross margin—up 820 basis points year-over-year and 450 sequentially. This came from scale efficiencies dropping fixed costs per kWh by 22% at over 95% factory utilization, firm pricing at $182 per kWh for Megapack thanks to 4680 cell density advantages, and a premium mix with Megapack at 32.5% margins from Autobidder AI software stacking arbitrage, regulation, and capacity revenues. Operating expenses were $90 million or 5.6% of revenue, driving 21.9% EBITDA margins—our highest—and contributing 35% of company-wide adjusted EBITDA despite just 18% of revenue.  

By region, the Americas led with 62% or $992 million, up 210%, boosted by IRA tax credits totaling over $1.2 billion year-to-date, hyperscaler data center deals, a 2.5 GWh Texas Megapack for ERCOT stability, and PG&E VPPs aggregating 150,000 Powerwalls. EMEA added 24% or $384 million, up 140%, with Berlin's 1.8 GWh supporting TenneT frequency response and Autobidder earning €45 million in ancillaries. APAC was 14% or $224 million, up 95%, offset by a 4 GWh Southeast Asia Megapack order for renewables integration.  

Key initiatives include Q4 Shanghai ramps to 10 GWh per quarter, Texas Megafactory Phase 2 by year-end targeting 100 GWh annually by 2026, Powerwall 4 rollout with 15% more capacity and 98% efficiency inverters, Prismatica solid-state cell pilots promising 2x cycle life and 30% LCOS cuts, Autobidder V2.5 live on 80% of deployments generating $70 million recurring, and Supercharger V4 V2G trials. Q4 guidance is $1.9 to $2.1 billion in energy revenue with 28.5 to 30.0% margins; full-year targets hold at $6.5 to $7 billion and 26%+ margins, scaling to $25 billion-plus by 2026.  

Now, turning to gross margin percentage and trends, a key profitability metric. Our consolidated gross margin hit 23.8%, up 550 basis points year-over-year from 18.3% and 370 sequentially from 20.1%. Excluding $180 million in regulatory credits or 110 basis points, automotive gross margin was 22.7%, the highest since Texas Gigafactory scale-up in 2022.  

Volume scale drove this: 125,000 units produced at 92% utilization across Texas, Nevada, Shanghai, and Berlin Gigafactories, yielding $3.2 billion automotive revenue at $48,200 ASPs with a premium mix shift. Fixed costs fell 28% per unit, aided by Nevada's unibody gigacasting at 1,200 parts per minute, saving $450 per vehicle with our 9,000-ton machines.  

Variable costs dropped sharply. Batteries at 42% of COGS reached $62 per kWh pack-level, down 21% via cell-to-pack architecture boosting density to 185 Wh/kg, lithium hedging at $12,000 per ton with Albemarle and Australian JV, and 20% silicon-doped anodes cutting costs 8% with 10% range gains. Powertrain costs declined 18% to $4,200 per vehicle using axial-flux motors at 95% efficiency and half the rare earths. Semiconductor prices fell 14% quarter-over-quarter; overall COGS per unit hit $37,100 from $40,800.  

Product mix added 240 basis points: Premium VoltX and TerraVolt at 38% volume versus 25% last year, with $62,000 ASPs; TerraVolt's 800V truck hit 15,000 units. Pricing discipline held—no North America discounts, IRA rebates boosting realized ASPs 12%; Europe parity despite imports.  

Regionally: North America at 26.2% automotive margin, up 680 basis points, beating Tesla's 19.9%; Europe 21.5%, up 420 despite ASP pressure, Berlin aiding; China/APAC 17.8%, prioritizing 65% volume growth to 37,000 units.  

Quarterly trends show inflection: Q3'23 at 18.3% consolidated, 17.2% auto ex-credits due to chips; Q4'23 19.6%/18.5% from Texas scale; Q1'24 20.4%/19.2% battery costs; Q2'24 20.1%/19.0% mix; Q3'24 23.8%/22.7% from gigacasting and cells.  

Forward, we target 25%+ automotive margins by 2025 end via 80% in-house batteries including QuantumScape solid-state at 400 Wh/kg, NovaPilot autonomy at $120 monthly subscriptions and 95% uptake adding $8,000 ASP at 85% margins, unboxed manufacturing for 30% COGS cuts, and supplier diversification. Q4 automotive margins 24.0-24.5% ex-credits on 140,000 deliveries. Long-term, 30%+ structural margins fund $15 billion capex for 2.5 million capacity as EVs hit 40% share by 2030.  

Before we open the line for Q&A, I'd like to hand over to our CTO, Dr. Raj Patel, for a deep dive into our electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains. These have driven our record Q3 deliveries and 8% ASP uplift from premium variants. Raj?  

Dr. Raj Patel:  
Thanks, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. At Voltara, we've achieved transformative advances in EV range and efficiency, tackling the top consumer concern—range anxiety, cited by 62% of buyers in J.D. Power's latest APEAL study. Our efforts on the Voltara One platform, powering the V1 Sedan and V1X SUV, have delivered industry-leading results, lifting gross margins to 28.5% from 22% a year ago via lower cost per mile.  

The numbers: Fleet-wide EPA range averaged 385 miles in Q3, up 28% from 300 miles last year. Real-world tests with Recurrent achieved 92% of EPA—best-in-class against Tesla Model Y's 88% and Rivian R1S's 85%. Efficiency improved to 198 Wh per mile, down 18% from 242, cutting total ownership costs 15% over 100,000 miles at $0.14 per kWh U.S. residential rates.  

Key initiatives: First, battery architecture. Our scaled 800V system uses CATL LFP-Prismatic cells at 245 Wh/kg, up from 190 in prior NMC packs, enabling 10-80% charging in 18 minutes on 350 kW DC—on par with Porsche Taycan. Silicon-graphene anodes from our Sila JV boost density 22%, fitting 102 kWh in 495 liters with 92% capacity after 500 cycles at full depth.  

Second, powertrain. Magnax axial-flux motors hit 97.2% peak efficiency, saving 5 Wh per mile over permanent magnets. SiC inverters at 99% efficiency keep drivetrain losses under 4%. AI torque vectoring via OTA V3.2 firmware improved highway efficiency 7%, validated on 1.2 million fleet miles.  

Third, aerodynamics and thermal. V1X SUV's 0.23 Cd uses active flaps and underbody panels, nearing Lucid Air. Glycol-free Valeo heat pumps hold 95% efficiency to -10°C, key for EU WLTP at 620 km—12% ahead of VW ID.7. Vapor chamber cooling limits cells to 35°C in heat, saving 2% range.  

Regionally, North America EPA gains made us #3 in U.S. EV sales; V1 outsold Hyundai Ioniq 6 by 15% in California. Europe WLTP underruns EPA by 5% with Continental EcoContact tires at 5.8 N/kN. China Shanghai adaptations yield 550 km CLTC at 20% lower $62 per kWh, grabbing 8% premium share vs. BYD Seal.  

These stem from $1.2 billion 2024 R&D, cutting COGS per kWh 22% to $87 via cell integration, with range premiums adding $4,500 ASP. Ahead, Voltara Two in Q4 2025 eyes 500+ EPA miles with Solid Power semi-solid-state at 375 Wh/kg and V2G for $150 million annual grid revenue by 2027. We're closing on Tesla Model S while undercutting price, outpacing GM Ultium at 220 Wh/mi. Lithium volatility up 12% QoQ is hedged multi-chemistry.  

In short, range and efficiency form our competitive moat, driving 65% repeat intent per NPS and setting us for 250,000 deliveries in 2025. Back to you, Sarah.  

Sarah Chen:  
Excellent overview, Raj. Operator, we're now ready for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.  

Analyst 1 (John Smith):  
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Elena, can you expand on competitive dynamics in North America, especially with Tesla's new affordable model rumors and Ford's ramp? How do your range improvements position Voltara?  

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Thanks, John. Absolutely, North America remains our largest market, and our 385-mile fleet average EPA range, with real-world 92% attainment, directly addresses consumer priorities. We've leapfrogged many rivals through 800V architecture and SiC powertrains, enabling faster charging and lower TCO. Against Tesla's rumored compact, our V1 Sedan's pricing and 7% OTA efficiency gains give us an edge in premium mass-market. Ford's ramp has been solid, but our gigacasting scale keeps costs lower. We're gaining share, #3 in U.S. EVs, and expect to hold momentum with TerraVolt trucks.  

Operator:  
Our next question from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley.  

Analyst 2 (Maria Lopez):  
Great, thanks. Sarah, on software—impressive growth, but with China regs tightening on data, how sustainable is the 210% YoY there? Any impact on ADS margins?  

Sarah Chen:  
Hi Maria, solid question. China's 25% segment share at $155 million reflects our localization strengths—Baidu JV maps and WeChat payments drive $15 ARPU. Regs are navigable with on-device processing via ElectroNet chips, minimizing cloud data flows. We've maintained 88% gross margins there, same as global, and expect continued acceleration as XNGP competition spurs innovation. No near-term drag; it's a growth engine.  

Operator:  
Our next question from David Kim with JPMorgan.  

Analyst 3 (David Kim):  
Thanks. Elena, on energy—$28 billion backlog is huge. With data center demand surging, any updates on hyperscaler wins or V2G synergies with autos?  

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
David, energy is diversifying us beautifully. We've secured additional hyperscaler contracts leveraging IRA credits, building on the Texas 2.5 GWh ERCOT deal. V2G trials with Powerwall 4 and Superchargers V4 integrate seamlessly with our fleet, unlocking fleet-scale grid services. Autobidder's multi-market stacking adds high-margin recurring revenue, synergizing auto and energy—expect $100 million from V2G adjacencies in H1 2025.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.  

Operator:  
Our final question from Lisa Chen with Barclays.  

Analyst 4 (Lisa Chen):  
Thanks, team. Sarah, gross margin trajectory to 25%+—what's the biggest risk if lithium spikes further, and how does unboxed manufacturing factor in?  

Sarah Chen:  
Lisa, thanks. Lithium hedging through 2025 at $12,000/ton with multi-chemistry (60% LFP) shields us from spot volatility. Unboxed process, debuting Q2 2025, targets 30% COGS reduction via robotic mega-assembly, accelerating our path to 30% structural margins. Q4 guide assumes stable FX; we're confident in execution.  

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Dr. Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.  

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident that Voltara Motors is well-positioned for continued success in the rapidly evolving automotive landscape. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
